full_text_en:
Tianjin International Trust and Investment Corporation v. Guangzhou Guoxin Property Development Company and Guangzhou International Trust and Investment Corporation — Dispute over Loan Contract (Appeal)

Appellant (Original Defendant): Guangzhou Guoxin Property Development Company.
Legal Representative: Wan Qianli, Manager of the Company.
Agent ad litem: Zhao Weiguang, Attorney at Beijing Century Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Sun Hongchi, Attorney at Tianjin Kaiming Law Firm.

Respondent (Original Plaintiff): Tianjin International Trust and Investment Corporation.
Legal Representative: Zhang Changjiu, General Manager of the Company.
Agents ad litem: Hou Weimin, Li Sijie, Staff Members of the Credit Department of the Company.

Original Defendant: Guangzhou International Trust and Investment Corporation.
Legal Representative: Xu Zhi, Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Company.

The appellant, Guangzhou Guoxin Property Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou Property), appealed to the Supreme People's Court against the judgment of first instance rendered by the Tianjin High People's Court in the case of dispute over a loan contract with the respondent, Tianjin International Trust and Investment Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Tianjin International Trust), and the original defendant, Guangzhou International Trust and Investment Corporation (hereinafter referred to as Guangzhou International Trust).

Facts Found by the Court of First Instance: On October 15, 1997, Tianjin International Trust and Guangzhou Property entered into the Trust Fund Loan Contract No. Jin Zi 97041. The contract provided that Tianjin International Trust would provide a trust fund loan of RMB 36.5 million to Guangzhou Property as special-purpose working capital. The term was six months, from October 29, 1997, to April 29, 1998, with an annual interest rate of 10.098%. If Guangzhou Property failed to repay the loan on the date specified in the contract, Tianjin International Trust was entitled to collect the loan from Guangzhou Property's deposit account. For overdue repayment, an additional 20% penalty interest would be charged based on the number of days overdue and the interest rate specified in the loan contract; if the overdue period exceeded three months, an additional 50% penalty interest would be charged on the loan interest rate. Guangzhou International Trust issued an irrevocable letter of guarantee for this contract, undertaking to unconditionally pay on behalf of Tianjin International Trust if the borrower failed to repay the loan principal, interest, and any payable penalties on time for any reason. On the same day, Tianjin International Trust and Guangzhou Property also entered into a Trust Deposit Agreement, stipulating that Guangzhou Property would deposit RMB 16.5 million with Tianjin International Trust for a term of six months, from October 29, 1997, to April 29, 1998. The deposit interest rate was calculated according to the demand deposit rate prescribed by the People's Bank of China, i.e., an annual interest rate of 1.98%. During the deposit term, Guangzhou Property could not use the deposit, and upon maturity, Guangzhou Property would entrust Tianjin International Trust to withdraw the deposit and use it for repayment.

After the execution of the above two contracts, Tianjin International Trust fulfilled its obligations in accordance with the contracts and lent RMB 36.5 million to Guangzhou Property. Upon the maturity of the contracts, on April 29, 1998, Guangzhou Property repaid the principal of RMB 16.5 million and paid the interest on the principal of RMB 36.5 million accrued up to March 20, 1998. The remaining amount has not been paid to date. Guangzhou International Trust also failed to perform its guarantee obligations. Tianjin International Trust filed a lawsuit with the Tianjin High People's Court to recover the said amounts and the expenses incurred in pursuing the debt, requesting a judgment ordering Guangzhou Property to repay the outstanding loan principal and interest of RMB 22,121,042, and ordering Guangzhou International Trust to assume joint and several liability for the repayment of the above debt of Guangzhou Property, as well as to bear the litigation costs.

The Tianjin High People's Court held: The Trust Fund Loan Contract signed between Tianjin International Trust and Guangzhou Property was voluntarily entered into on an equal footing between the parties and did not violate the provisions of national laws or regulations. It should be deemed valid. According to Article 89 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China, a contract lawfully established is protected by law. Guangzhou Property failed to perform its repayment obligations in accordance with the contract. According to Article 112 of the General Principles of the Civil Law, it should bear liability for breach of contract. Regarding the liability for breach of contract in the loan contract, the provision that if the overdue period exceeds three months, an additional 50% interest will be charged on the loan interest rate exceeded the regulation of the People's Bank of China that the penalty interest for overdue loan repayment is 0.04% per day. Therefore, the penalty interest should be calculated at 0.04% per day. The expression of intent by Guangzhou International Trust to issue the joint and several liability guarantee was genuine and should be deemed valid. As it failed to perform its obligations as stipulated in the guarantee, according to Article 18 of the Guarantee Law of the People's Republic of China, it should bear joint and several liability for repayment. Accordingly, the court rendered the following judgment: 1. Guangzhou Property shall pay Tianjin International Trust the loan principal of RMB 20 million, the interest within the term of RMB 373,230, and the corresponding penalty interest (from April 29, 1998, to July 29, 1998, calculated at an annual rate of 12.118%; from July 29, 1998, until the date of payment, calculated at a daily rate of 0.04%); 2. Guangzhou International Trust shall assume joint and several liability for repayment of the above items; 3. The above payments shall be made within 10 days after this judgment takes effect; for overdue payments, execution shall be carried out in accordance with Article 232 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China; 4. Other claims are dismissed. The case acceptance fee was RMB 120,615, and the preservation fee was RMB 111,120, to be borne by Guangzhou Property and Guangzhou International Trust, each in the amount of RMB 115,867.5.

Guangzhou Property, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the Tianjin High People's Court, appealed to the Supreme People's Court, claiming: The actual principal of the loan contract in this case was RMB 20 million. The RMB 16.5 million remained in Tianjin International Trust's own account and was not used, but interest was calculated on RMB 36.5 million. The loan contract and the deposit contract should be viewed together; the deposit was an additional condition for the loan, which constituted an act to circumvent the law. Furthermore, the provision on penalty interest in the loan contract did not comply with the regulations of the People's Bank of China and should be modified. Tianjin International Trust responded: The two contracts are two independent legal relationships. It was possible that the loan of RMB 36.5 million was granted, but only RMB 20 million was used, with the remaining RMB 16.5 million temporarily unused and deposited with the company for future use.

Additional Facts Found by the Supreme People's Court: On October 29, 1997, Tianjin International Trust actually disbursed RMB 20 million to Guangzhou Property, while the other RMB 16.5 million remained with Tianjin International Trust. On March 20, 1998, Guangzhou Property paid interest within the contract term of RMB 1,330,824 based on the loan amount of RMB 36.5 million.

The Supreme People's Court held: The loan contract signed between the parties in this case was voluntarily negotiated and entered into on an equal footing. Except for the provision on penalty interest, which violates the regulations of the People's Bank of China and should be deemed invalid, the other clauses do not violate national laws and regulations and should be deemed legally valid. According to Article 6 of the Economic Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, an economic contract, once lawfully established, is legally binding, and the parties must fully perform the obligations stipulated in the contract. On the same day, the parties also signed a deposit contract. Although it was stipulated that Guangzhou Property would deposit RMB 16.5 million directly with Tianjin International Trust, in fact, Guangzhou Property did not deposit any funds with Tianjin International Trust. Instead, Tianjin International Trust directly deducted RMB 16.5 million from the loan amount of RMB 36.5 million and only disbursed RMB 20 million to Guangzhou Property, while charging interest on the full RMB 36.5 million loan. The intention of the parties in signing the deposit contract was to enable Tianjin International Trust to obtain the difference between the demand deposit interest rate and the loan interest rate, thereby increasing the interest rate on the aforementioned RMB 20 million loan. This act was aimed at circumventing legal provisions. According to Article 7, Paragraph 1 of the Economic Contract Law, it constitutes a contract that violates laws and administrative regulations and should be deemed invalid. Both parties bear responsibility for this invalid deposit contract. Since the actual loan disbursed under the loan contract was RMB 20 million, the interest within the contract term should be calculated based on the principal of RMB 20 million. The excess portion of the interest within the contract term already paid by Guangzhou Property should be offset against the actual loan principal. Guangzhou Property's ground of appeal that the deposit contract was an act to circumvent the law is valid and is supported by this court. The irrevocable letter of guarantee issued by Guangzhou International Trust for the loan contract in this case was a genuine expression of intent and did not violate legal provisions; it should be deemed a valid guarantee. According to Article 21 of the Guarantee Law, Guangzhou International Trust shall assume guarantee liability for Guangzhou Property's debt in this case. The original judgment's findings on certain facts were unclear, and the calculation standard for overdue penalty interest was inappropriate; it should be appropriately modified. Accordingly, in accordance with Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items 1 and 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Supreme People's Court renders the following judgment:

1. Affirm Items 2, 3, and 4 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (1998) Gao Jing Yi Chu Zi No. 37 of the Tianjin High People's Court;

2. Modify Item 1 of the said civil judgment, which reads: "The Defendant, Guangzhou Property Development Company, shall pay the Plaintiff, Tianjin International Trust and Investment Corporation, the loan principal of RMB 20 million, the interest within the term of RMB 373,230, and the corresponding penalty interest (from April 29, 1998, to July 29, 1998, calculated at an annual rate of 12.118%; from July 29, 1998, until the date of payment, calculated at a daily rate of 0.04%)" to read: Guangzhou Guoxin Property Development Company shall pay Tianjin International Trust and Investment Corporation the loan principal of RMB 19,678,976 and pay penalty interest on that amount (calculated from April 29, 1998, until the date of payment, based on the standard penalty interest rate for overdue loan repayment prescribed by the People's Bank of China for the corresponding period).

The case acceptance fees for the first instance and second instance in this case are each RMB 120,615. Guangzhou Guoxin Property Development Company shall bear RMB 67,008.33 for each instance, and Tianjin International Trust and Investment Corporation shall bear RMB 53,606.67 for each instance. The property preservation fee of RMB 111,120 shall be borne by Guangzhou Guoxin Property Development Company.
